claims.text: Rare-earth doping of YBa2Cu3O7 at concentrations up to 0.3 mol will enhance its superconducting transition temperature.
Rare-earth doping may broaden the superconducting region relative to undoped YBa2Cu3O7.
Polycrystalline YBa2Cu3O7 is superconducting under standard conditions.
Polycrystalline YBa2Cu3O7 has a critical temperature of approximately 90 K under standard conditions.
Rare-earth elements will be substituted into the YBa2Cu3O7 lattice over a nominal range of 0 to 0.3 mol using solid-state synthesis at 900°C.
The rare-earth dopants partially replace Y ions in the YBa2Cu3O7 lattice.
Partial rare-earth substitution creates local lattice distortions.
Partial rare-earth substitution can change oxygen doping and oxygen ordering.
Changes in local distortion, oxygen doping, and oxygen ordering affect superconducting pathways.
Rare-earth ions can modify the lattice parameters and local bonding environment of YBa2Cu3O7.
Modified lattice parameters and local bonding environments influence electron-pairing interactions.
Modified lattice parameters and local bonding environments influence the density of states near the Fermi level.
Changes to electron pairing and the density of states enhance superconductivity.
Rare-earth doping will increase Tc by a few kelvins relative to undoped YBa2Cu3O7.
Rare-earth doping may expand the superconducting temperature range.
Undoped YBa2Cu3O7 has a typical Tc of approximately 90 K and a well-defined superconducting transition.
Doping levels above 0.3 mol or poorly controlled sintering may cause second-phase formation.
Second-phase formation may be detrimental to superconductivity.
Quantitative Tc changes and structure-property correlations beyond 0.3 mol doping are not well established.
The hypothesis is refuted if doping up to 0.3 mol fails to increase Tc or reduces superconductivity relative to undoped YBa2Cu3O7.
